stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 6 \ln\left(1 + \frac{x + 4}{2}\right) \). The Taylor series for f about \( x = -4 \) is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{6 (-1)^{n+1} \left(x + 4\right)^{n}}{n \cdot 2^{n}} \). Does the series converge to f at \( x = -2 \)? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: Yes, because \( x = -2 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( -6 < x \le -2 \) includes.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x + 4\right| < 2 \), the interior \( -6 < x < -2 \), and \( x = -2 \) is an endpoint.
At \( x = -2 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{6 (-1)^{n+1}}{n} \), which converges by the alternating series test, so the interval of convergence is \( -6 < x \le -2 \).
